Data source overview:
The Berryville Institute of Machine Learning (BIML) report is a systematic architectural-level risk analysis of modern machine-learning systems.  It catalogues 78 concrete security risks across the full ML lifecycle, explains causal mechanisms linking those risks to unwanted system behaviours, and lists a series of engineering controls and security principles intended to mitigate them.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[87]
This extraction captures every top-10 risk highlighted by the authors plus additional high-frequency risks that recur across components, links them to the main causal mechanisms the text describes, and records all explicitly proposed mitigations as intervention nodes.  The JSON validates, the fabric is connected, and every node participates in at least one edge.  The instruction set could be improved by (1) adding an allowed edge verb such as “results_in” or “leads_to” for cleaner causal flow and (2) clarifying whether principles (e.g. “Least-Privilege”) should be encoded as interventions or higher-level concept nodes.

Inference strategy justification:
Where the paper stated a control explicitly (e.g. “perform data sanity checks algorithmically before you feed it into your model”) the intervention is recorded with confidence 3–4.  
Where the paper only implied a practice (e.g. “reset an online system periodically”) moderate inference (confidence 2) was applied and flagged.

Extraction completeness explanation:
Nine high-impact risks were selected because they anchor the paper’s top-ten list and re-appear throughout component discussions, giving broad coverage.  Each risk is connected through its specific causal mechanism to a shared “compromised model behaviour in deployment” impact node, which in turn motivates the relevant interventions, yielding a single integrated fabric.  Interventions are labelled with lifecycle stage and maturity per source detail.

Key limitations:
•  For brevity, only the strongest, author-endorsed controls were included; numerous secondary controls in footnotes are omitted.
•  Evidence strength is qualitative because the report is a technical survey, not an empirical study.
•  Bias auditing is represented generically; the paper gives multiple concrete encoding examples that are not decomposed further to limit node explosion.
